info.name: Personal Management API
info.description:
API collection for the Personal Management app.

**Setup**
1. Import `personal-management.postman_environment.json` and select it.
2. Fill `supabase_anon_key` (from `.env`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` / publishable key), `email`, `password`.
3. Run **Auth > Login**. It saves `auth_token` (valid ~1 hour). Every request inherits `Bearer {{auth_token}}` from the collection.

**Conventions**
- Running routes return errors as `{ error, message }`, validation errors as `{ error, issues }`.
- Requests are rate limited per user (429 when exceeded).

**Coverage**
- [x] Running > Activities
- [ ] Running: dashboard, analytics, gear, goals, races, health, AI, sync
- [ ] Inventory
- [ ] Trading
- [ ] Investment Flow
- [x] Auth: login, logout, Strava connection
- [x] Notifications
- [ ] User Settings

item.name: Auth
item.description: Get a Supabase session token for the other requests.

request.description: Signs in with Supabase and saves `access_token` to `auth_token`.

One-time: adds an email + password login to an account that signs in with GitHub. Put a fresh `auth_token` (copied from the browser session) first, set `new_password` as a local (current) value only, then send. After this, **Login (Supabase password)** works.

If Supabase answers with a reauthentication / nonce error, log out and log in with GitHub again, then retry with the new token.
Signs the current session out on the server. After this the `auth_token` stops working.

item.name: Strava
item.description: Strava connection and sync (`app/api/running/v1/auth/strava`). Note: these routes use mixed error shapes (some `{ error }` only).

request.description: **Browser flow, not for Postman.** Sets a state cookie and 302-redirects to `https://www.strava.com/oauth/authorize` (scope `read,activity:read_all,profile:read_all`). Open it in the browser while logged in.

**Called by Strava, not by you.** Public route (no auth header). Checks `state` against the cookie, exchanges `code`, saves credentials, then 302-redirects back into the app (or to an error page / `/login`).
Removes the Strava connection. Activities already imported are kept.
Pulls new Strava activities since the last sync. On the very first sync (no `last_sync_at`) it starts the background backfill instead.

response.name: Backfill started
Needs reconnect

request.description: Queues a `strava/fetch-streams` job for every Strava activity to backfill detail fields. Async: returns the number queued.
Recomputes derived metrics (aerobic decoupling, efficiency factor, VO2max estimate). `force=true` recomputes every activity, otherwise only ones missing metrics.

item.name: Activities
item.description:
Running activities: list, detail, manual entry, edit, delete, streams.

All routes check ownership (`user_id`). Another user's activity id returns 404.

request.description: Each item now also has `has_garmin` (boolean) and `training_effect_label` (Garmin label or `null`). `source` can be `strava`, `garmin`, `manual`, ... A `garmin` run has no gear, best efforts, map or splits.

request.description: Distinct `activity_type` values the user has, sorted. Use it to fill the type filter.

Creates an activity with `source = manual`.

**Required:** `started_at` (ISO datetime), `duration_sec` (int > 0), `distance_m` (> 0).

**Optional:** `activity_type` (`easy` | `tempo` | `interval` | `long` | `race` | `recovery`), `perceived_exertion` (1–10), `notes` (max 2000), `avg_hr` / `max_hr` (30–250), `avg_cadence` (0–300), `avg_pace_sec_per_km`, `max_pace_sec_per_km`, `elevation_gain_m`, `elevation_loss_m`, `calories`, `moving_time_sec`.

**Duplicate check:** returns 409 when an activity already starts within ±5 minutes and its distance is within ±200 m.

response.name: Validation failed

request.description:
Same as **Activities > Get activity detail**, plus:
- `garmin`: Garmin metrics, or `null` when no Garmin activity is linked
- `activity.data_sources`: `{ primary, garmin_linked, perceived_exertion_from }`

Merge rules: Garmin wins for physiology and running dynamics. Strava wins for map, streams, splits, best efforts, gear, social. `perceived_exertion` is filled from `garmin.rpe` only when the user has not set it. Fields the watch does not support are `null`.

request.description:
Re-runs matching (start time within 60s, distance within 2%) when the activity is not linked yet, then re-fetches the Garmin metrics. `perceived_exertion` is filled from Garmin RPE only when it is empty.

Rate limited with the `sync` tier. A 429 can also mean Garmin itself is rate limiting.

response.name: Garmin rate limited

request.description:
Edits notes, type, or RPE. At least one field is required.

`activity_type`: `easy` | `tempo` | `interval` | `long` | `race` | `recovery`. `perceived_exertion`: 1–10. `notes`: max 2000 chars.

response.name: Empty body

request.description:
Deletes one activity (child rows like splits, laps, streams go with it).

Uses `manual_activity_id` (set by **Create manual activity**) so you don't delete a Strava run by accident.

Time-series data for charts and the map, downsampled in the database.

`resolution`: `raw` | `10s` (default) | `30s` | `60s`.

Point fields: `t` (seconds from start), `dist_m`, `hr`, `cadence`, `alt`, `pace` (sec/km), `velocity` (m/s), `lat`, `lng`. Activities without streams return `data: []` and `total_points: 0`.

⚠️ **Destructive.** Deletes every running activity of the user (plus splits, laps, streams, best efforts). Cannot be undone.

Body must be exactly `{ "confirmation": "DELETE" }`.

response.name: Missing confirmation

item.name: Garmin connection
item.description: Garmin Personal API key for the Running settings card (#922). The key is stored encrypted and never returned.

request.description:
The API key is never returned, only `key_last4` and expiry.

`status`: `not_connected` | `connected` | `expired` | `invalid`. `expired` is worked out from `key_expires_at` (the key works through the whole expiry day). Timestamps come back as `+00:00`.

Validates the key by exchanging it for a Garmin access token, then stores it encrypted. Nothing is stored when Garmin rejects the key or is down.

`expires_at` = expiry date chosen in Garmin Connect (`YYYY-MM-DD`, today up to 1 year ahead).

When the previous status was `expired` or `invalid`, a catch-up sync starts on its own from the last successful sync (max 90 days, 7 days if never synced).

response.name: Validation failed

request.description: Deletes the stored key and cached token. Garmin metrics already linked to activities are kept.

item.name: Sync
item.description: Strava and Garmin sync state and triggers.

request.description:
Strava connection plus the Garmin state. `connected` and `last_sync_at` are unchanged (Strava). `garmin` has the same shape as **Garmin connection > Get Garmin connection**.

If the Garmin lookup fails on the server, `garmin` is `null` and the Strava part still returns 200. Treat `null` like "unknown", not like `not_connected`.

This read uses the normal rate-limit tier. The sync triggers (`POST sync/garmin`, `POST sync/strava`) stay in the stricter `sync` tier (15 per hour).

response.name: Garmin expiring soon (14 days or less)

request.description:
Queues a background job: links Garmin activities to existing ones and imports Garmin runs missing in our DB (`source = garmin`).

Body is optional (defaults to the last 7 days, `to` never goes past today). Max range 90 days. Only one sync runs at a time per user. Rate limited with the `sync` tier.

503 means the job could not be queued (for example the Inngest Dev Server is not running locally). The sync lock is released, so the call can be repeated.

response.name: Range over 90 days
Already running
Background jobs unavailable

item.name: Notifications
item.description:
In-app notifications, push subscriptions and per-type push preferences (`app/api/notifications/v1`).

Errors use `{ error, message }`. List validation errors use `{ error, issues }`.

request.description:
Newest first.

| Query | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `page` | 1 | ≥ 1 |
| `limit` | 20 | 1–50 (400 above 50) |
| `status` | `all` | `all` \| `unread` \| `read` |

Paging past the last page returns an empty `items` array, not an error.

response.name: Success
Validation failed

request.description: Number of unread notifications, for the bell badge.
Body: `{ "id": <positive integer> }` (strings are coerced). Only the user's own notifications.

response.name: Validation failed

request.description: Marks every unread notification of the user as read. No body.

One entry per type, defaulting to `push_enabled: true` when never saved.

Types: post_activity, weekly_review, friday_prep, anomaly, race_reminder, product_update, low_stock, pr_achieved, gear_mileage, strava_disconnected, restock_reminder, event_analysis_ready, weekly_summary, session_ended.

response.name: Success

request.description: Body: `type` (one of: post_activity, weekly_review, friday_prep, anomaly, race_reminder, product_update, low_stock, pr_achieved, gear_mileage, strava_disconnected, restock_reminder, event_analysis_ready, weekly_summary, session_ended) and `push_enabled` (boolean).

response.name: Bad push_enabled

item.name: Push subscriptions
item.description: Web Push devices for the user.

request.description: Registered devices plus the last successful and last failed delivery, and endpoint hashes reported expired recently.

Registers (or refreshes) this browser's PushSubscription. `endpoint` must be a supported push service URL (max 2048). `keys.p256dh` max 200, `keys.auth` max 100.

The session is confirmed with the Auth server. 409 when the endpoint already belongs to another account with different keys.

response.name: Unsupported endpoint
Other account

request.description: Removes one of the user's devices by its UUID.
Sends a test notification to one subscribed endpoint of the user. A 200 can still mean the push failed: check `data.sent`.

response.name: Invalid endpoint
Not subscribed
